headline: Halluminate raises $30 million to build AI training environments for financial work
body: Halluminate, a nine-person San Francisco startup building AI training environments for financial work, has raised $30 million in a Series A led by Oak HC/FT, bringing its total funding to $38.5 million. On its August benchmark, seven frontier models worked through a simulated due-diligence process for a company acquisition, and the highest average score was 51%. CEO Jerry Wu told Fortune that four of the top five closed-source U.S. AI labs are paying customers.
note: A top score of 51% on deal due-diligence tasks is a useful reality check for banks and private-equity firms weighing AI agents: the agents struggled to carry instructions through to the final deliverable.

evidence.text: Halluminate, a nine-person San Francisco startup building AI training environments for financial work, has raised $30 million in a Series A led by Oak HC/FT, bringing its total funding to $38.5 million.
A benchmark released by the company in August asked seven frontier models to work through a simulated company-acquisition due-diligence process.

Across the benchmark, agents struggled to carry instructions through to the final deliverable: They left out required changes, used the wrong analytical method, or relied on information that had been superseded.
According to Wu, four of the top five closed-source U.S. AI labs are paying customers.
Simulating an investment banker’s work is fundamentally different from simulating a software engineer’s work, CEO Jerry Wu tells Fortune
